plain_language_overview: The court has temporarily stopped further tree cutting at East Potomac Golf Course through October 26 and requires advance notice before the government makes other irreversible changes. The court has not yet decided whether longer-term relief should be granted. An evidentiary hearing on the preliminary-injunction request is scheduled for October 19.

orders_in_effect.title: Temporary halt on further tree cutting
orders_in_effect.summary: The federal defendants may not fell additional trees at East Potomac Golf Course through October 26, 2026, unless the court enters a further order.
orders_in_effect.source_label: October 13 minute order; Docket entry 79 memorandum opinion

orders_in_effect.title: Advance notice required for irreversible changes
orders_in_effect.summary: Through October 26, the government must give the court and the plaintiffs three business days' written notice before making an irreversible modification to a permanent form or feature of the golf course.

decided_issues.title: Emergency temporary restraining order granted
decided_issues.summary: On the limited record then before it, the court found that the plaintiffs had shown likely success on jurisdiction and their NEPA claim, likely irreparable harm, and equities favoring temporary relief. This was a preliminary ruling, not a final decision on the lawsuit's merits.
decided_issues.source_label: October 13 minute order and Docket entry 79

decided_issues.title: Amended and supplemental complaint permitted
decided_issues.summary: The court allowed the plaintiffs to update their complaint because the facts surrounding the project were changing quickly. This ruling allowed the new allegations to be filed; it did not decide whether those allegations are ultimately correct.

pending_issues.title: Whether longer-term preliminary relief should be granted
pending_issues.summary: The plaintiffs' motion for a preliminary injunction and stay remains before the court. The temporary October 13 restrictions do not themselves resolve whether protections will continue for the remainder of the litigation.

pending_issues.title: Jurisdiction, final agency action, and the NEPA merits
pending_issues.summary: The parties continue to dispute whether the court has jurisdiction, whether there is reviewable final agency action, and whether the government complied with NEPA. The temporary restraining-order findings are preliminary and do not finally decide these questions.
pending_issues.source_label: Docket entries 80 and 84; October 18 minute order

pending_issues.title: Government request to disqualify the judge and release hearing audio
pending_issues.summary: The government filed a motion asking that the judge be disqualified and that audio be released. The docket supplied to the tracker does not show that this motion has been decided.

prior_actions.title: Short October 12 tree-removal halt
prior_actions.summary: The court initially stopped all tree removal until 7:00 a.m. on October 13 or further order. That short order was superseded by the October 13 temporary restraining order extending protection through October 26.

prior_actions.title: Earlier request for a stay or preliminary injunction deferred
prior_actions.summary: In May, the court deferred ruling on the earlier request for a stay or preliminary injunction while the parties completed additional briefing. Later factual developments produced the October emergency proceedings.

next_event.title: Preliminary-injunction evidentiary hearing
next_event.summary: The court is scheduled to hear evidence and argument concerning the request for longer-term preliminary relief. The hearing is set for Courtroom 12, with public telephone access except while sworn testimony is taken.
